en: **Title:** *Paramārthastava* (Hymn to the Ultimate Truth) **Author:** Nāgārjuna **Source:** Tola & Dragonetti, 1985, pp. 19–20 I bow down to the Buddha, who has transcended all extremes, Who is free from the net of conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), And who has taught the ultimate truth, Which is profound, peaceful, and beyond all discursive thought. The world is bound by the fetters of conceptual construction; It does not see the reality that is free from such construction. But for those who have seen reality as it is, There is no bondage, nor is there liberation. The various views regarding self and phenomena Are all merely the fabrications of the mind. Since they do not exist in the ultimate sense, They are like a dream or a magical illusion. When the mind is purified of all conceptualization, One realizes the state that is beyond all expression. This is the peace, the cessation of suffering, The ultimate goal of the noble ones. Thus, having understood this ultimate truth, One should abandon all attachment to views. For those who dwell in the non-conceptual, There is neither birth nor death, neither coming nor going. May all beings, through this realization, Attain the supreme state of peace. This is the hymn to the ultimate truth, Composed by the venerable Nāgārjuna.
How shall I praise you, O Protector, who are unarisen and without abode?
He has transcended worldly analogies and lies beyond the range of the path of speech.
Nevertheless, according to the nature of your sphere within the reality of suchness,
I shall praise the Guru with devotion by resorting to worldly designations.
Since you possess the nature of the unarisen, arising does not exist for you;
there is neither going nor coming, O Protector—homage be to you who are without intrinsic nature!
You are neither an entity nor a non-entity, neither annihilated nor eternal.
You are neither eternal nor impermanent; homage be to you, the non-dual!
You are not red, green, or madder-colored; no color of yours is perceived.
You are neither yellow, black, nor white; homage be to you, the colorless!
You are neither great nor small, neither long nor circular;
you have attained the immeasurable state—homage be to you, the Immeasurable!
You are neither far nor near, neither in space nor upon the earth.
Homage be to you who do not abide in saṃsāra nor in nirvāṇa.
(7) Not abiding in any phenomena, having reached the realization of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), and having attained supreme profundity—homage be to you, the Profound One. (8)
Thus praised, may you be praised—or rather, what is the use of praise?
Since all phenomena are empty, who is praised, or by whom is anyone praised?
Who is able to fully praise you, who are devoid of arising and ceasing?
Having praised the Sugata, who is devoid of movement, and in whom neither end nor middle exists, and for whom neither grasper nor grasped is found,
nor going nor coming— by this merit, may this world proceed to the state of the Sugata.
The Praise of the Ultimate Truth is completed.
